q: Show that the unit of impulse, $\text{N}\cdot\text{s}$, is the same as the unit of momentum, $\text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$.
A train brakes steadily and stops. What is the direction of the impulse of the net braking force on the train, and what does its magnitude depend on?
a: The impulse points against the motion, in the same direction as the change in momentum. Its magnitude is the train's original momentum $mv$, so it depends on the mass and the initial velocity of the train and not on how long the braking takes.
